questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Tonga?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Tonga article.

questions.proof: The capital city of Nukuʻalofa is on Tongatapuon.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Tonga?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tonga article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Tonga are Tongan and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Tonga was no longer a protected state and became independent in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Tonga article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Tonga was no longer a protected state and became independent in 1970.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It became a member of the United Nations in September _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Tonga article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: It became a member of the United Nations in September 1999.
